title: Managed-site update script fails to load when an optional toolchain module is absent

problem.statement: The managed-site update entry point aborted before performing any work when it was executed from a reconstructed toolchain that did not ship one of its imported modules.
symptoms: Node exited with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any update logic ran
No machine-readable result document was produced
The failure occurred identically on every invocation, including dry-run
evidence_refs: validate-pack log: release pipeline phase 3 test failure

root_cause.statement: A static top-level ESM import created a hard load-time dependency on a module that the reconstructed toolchain deliberately does not copy, so module resolution failed before the entry point executed.
evidence_refs: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming the unresolved specifier and the importing file

fix.description: Load the optional module through a dynamic import at call time and declare it as part of the reconstructed toolchain, so resolution failure surfaces as a handled runtime error rather than preventing the script from loading.
fix.rationale: Load-time coupling made an optional capability fatal for every caller; call-time resolution keeps the failure diagnosable and scoped.

changes.summary: Replace the static import with a call-time dynamic import so the entry point stays loadable.
Declare the module directory as part of the toolchain the reconstruction copies.

results.detail: The previously failing rehydration test passed after the change.
Reproduced before the change and not reproduced after it.

causality.statement: The same suite failed before the change and passed after it, with no other change in the tree between the two runs.

conditions: Applies to Node ESM entry points executed from a reconstructed partial toolchain

limitations: Proven on a single project and a single Drupal core version
Verified through the repository test suite only, not under production load
Describes a tooling defect, not a Drupal core or contrib defect
notes: Captured as a deterministic fixture demonstrating the full solved-case contract.
